label: verify-bm-competing-approaches

claims.claim: The 3/2 ceiling is prior art (Holstov 2015 wrote the maximum stays at 1.5); the Lean file proves the bound and equality when m^2 n = 1, not the converse.
claims.source_says: Lean: theorem timoshenkoCoefficient_le (coefficient <= 3/(2h)); timoshenkoCoefficient_eq_of_optimal with hypothesis m^2*n = 1; no converse theorem present. Holstov source not fetched.
claims.note: The Lean half matches the file as written; the Holstov quote could not be opened (Newcastle page 403/202, DOI redirect only), so the prior-art half is unchecked.

claims.claim: The formula over-predicts maximum curvature of printed soft humidity bilayers about 4 times (5.3 vs 1.2 per mm; 1.6 vs about 0.4 per mm), though it follows trends.
claims.source_says: Maximum curvature predicted from a humidity dependent E PDOT:PSS is 5.3 mm–1. A maximum curvature of 1.2 mm–1 was reached, about three times the value of the 54 µm bilayer. ...a maximum curvature of 1.6 mm–1 could be calculated
claims.note: Numbers reproduce (5.3/1.2=4.4; 0.4 is derived from 'about three times'; 1.6/0.4=4.0); 'nicely predict the trends' is also in the text.

claims.claim: Tough 1000 CTE 161.6-168.2 vs Rigid 10K 41-48 um/m/C gives 0.45-0.51 % over 40 K, against 0.2 % estimated for humidity; so a temperature-by-humidity factorial is required.
claims.source_says: Tough 1000 datasheet: 'Thermal Expansion (0-150 C) ... 161.6 m/m/°C 168.2 m/m/°C'. Rigid 10K datasheet: 'Thermal Expansion, 0-150 °C' with '48 m/m/°C' visible; other values scrambled.
claims.note: Tough 1000 values confirmed and arithmetic reproduces (113.6-127.2 x 40 K = 0.45-0.51 %), but Rigid 10K range could not be read cleanly, the 0.2 % is an unmeasured estimate, and the factorial is a recommendation.

claims.claim: SMP bilayers move in about 20 s but need heat and are one-shot; kirigami needs external strain; hydrogel bilayers need 1-280 min and are soft.
claims.source_says: Ding: 'After ~20 s, the samples had completed the transformation'; 'remains largely unchanged upon further cooling and heating'. Kirigami: 'Pulling on the sheet in the axial direction'. Review: 'bending angle ... 20 to 720° with actuation times varying from 1 to 280 min'; modulus few to 100s of kPa.
claims.note: All four parts match their sources; heat need is from Ding's 62 C water immersion.

overall: Three of four key claims check out. The Holstov prior-art half of claim 1 could not be opened, so it is unchecked, and the Rigid 10K range in claim 3 could not be read cleanly. The Lean statement matches the file as written. The Dingler numbers and the 4x arithmetic reproduce.
